signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Divergence
signals.text: The G10 Currency Strength Scorecard shows CHF outperforming at +1.002% across 6 pairs while AUD lags at −0.628% across 4 pairs, yielding a 1.630% leader-to-laggard spread. AUD/CHF trades at 0.5544, positioned below its SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.5544 close vs SMA20 0.8303 area context; AUD/USD below SMA20 0.6844). Despite RBA at 4.85% vs SNB 0.00% offering a +485bp nominal carry advantage, safe-haven flows toward CHF dominate market pricing. Australia's ESI index stands at −13.0 compared to Switzerland's +28.0, confirming fundamental data divergence. Retail sentiment data retail positioning shows 83% of traders long AUD/CHF, creating a heavy contrarian unwinding risk against institutional momentum. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/CHF, driven by G10 bilateral divergence and safe-haven CHF demand. Catalyst: Australia CPI preview event (4.8% headline expected) in upcoming sessions. signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Carry vs Technical Resistance
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.29, maintaining a position above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (158.75/158.12/158.82). The 25d Risk Reversal reads −1.80, indicating strong put skew and heavy institutional demand for downside JPY protection despite Fed 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25% delivering a +275bp carry advantage (+269bp OIS carry premium via SOFR 3.92% vs TONA 1.23%). The pair approaches 160.00, the critical level where historical MoF verbal warnings intensify. CFTC data reveals JPY Leveraged Funds net short at −29,545 (pctl 85, z +1.12), signaling crowded carry positioning that leaves the pair vulnerable to sudden unwinds. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY, carry-supported while holding above SMA cluster. Catalyst: Tokyo Core CPI release (2.8% YoY forecast). Risk: VIX breaks above 30 or BoJ intervention materializes near 160.00, triggering a sharp positioning unwind.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Policy Divergence Repricing + Technical Breakdown
signals.text: Nomura revised its Bank of Canada call to a December rate hike following Governor Macklem's comments on viewing temporary supply shocks through policy, shifting BoC expectations against Fed 4.00% [ON HOLD] vs BoC 2.50% [HIKING]. USD/CAD trades at 1.4273, undergoing a counter-trend pullback with a bearish wide-range bar printed on the latest session while remaining above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (1.4169/1.4148/1.3931). CFTC Leveraged Funds net short CAD at −75,447 contracts (30.4% long), presenting squeeze potential as market pricing adjusts to a hawkish BoC stance. Retail positioning shows 81% of traders short USD/CAD, conflicting with short-term institutional repricing. Trade bias: Bearish USD/CAD, driven by hawkish BoC policy shift. Catalyst: US Core PCE release (3.1% YoY forecast) and US GDP data. Risk: US PCE inflation surprises significantly to the upside, solidifying Fed rate expectations and capping CAD gains.
